Adding sdbusplus maintainers and others for review.
Would this require any change to dbus-sensors or would those continue to work as such since you necessitating the need for a Type property for new Dbus paths?

It should depend on which value the ```Type``` property has in the nested records, if any.

In the current schemas the nested records like ```FirmwareInfoDef``` usually do not have their own ```Type``` property which means they should not be affected by this change. 

So the dbus tree should look the same and the code should work as before.


If then in the future someone wants to refactor a daemon in dbus-sensors to use the PDI generated code, enablement would look something like:

- Update the specific schema to require that ```Type``` field on the nested records.
- Create (or preferably, generate) the PDI interface definitions for the involved interfaces from the schemas involved
- Use some script to add ```Type``` property to all the nested records and array records of that specific configuration schema on all existing configurations
- Update the daemon to start consuming the interfaces which were newly added to the dbus tree via the generated clients.
- Profit
Normally i see all configuration interfaces have "Name" property as well but i suppose that can be generated by suffixing some index, @spinler@us.ibm.com is it required to have Name property or not?

The top-level configuration interfaces all have ```Name``` property which is used as part of the object path. But not all nested configuration interfaces have this property currently.

For example ```xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.SPIFlash.FirmwareInfo``` is top-level configuration based on object path, but has a nested interface name and no ```Name``` property.

And ```xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.ADC.Thresholds0``` may have ```Name == "upper critical"```. which is not unique.

So every exposes record currently should have one ```Name``` property on its primary (non-nested) dbus interface (feel free to correct me here 😊 )

Because the ```Name``` is part of the object path it has to be unique below the entity that it's exposed on. Not sure if it's unique across all entities, that would be hard to enforce since potentially any EM config could be probed. 

Various daemons currently use ```Name``` property to form their own object paths. For example the ADCSensor.
```
        |- /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VBAT_33
        |- /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VDD_12_RUN
        |- /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VDD_33_DUAL
        |- /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VDD_33_RUN
        |- /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VDD_5_DUAL
        `- /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VDD_5_RUN
```

So for that daemon, it actually forms the object path based on ```Name``` property on the configuration interface, not based on the object path.

Looks like some part of your comment got cut off here.

> I'm a little worried we're conflating the problem further here by creating more depth in paths.

## concern about configuration

Do you see the problem in how deep configuration is nested in json configs?
(which could be a concern about misrepresentation)

## concern about developer workflow (tree)

With the alternative code path, the dbus tree may be somewhat bloated since the json objects in arrays would get their own object path.

Maybe we could have a helper program there to list the object paths / configuration records for an entity? 

Like a custom ```busctl tree``` but specific to EM. What do you think 😊

## concern about developer workflow (introspecting)

With the alternative code path, it would not be as easy anymore for folks to dump some logs of ```busctl introspect``` to show all the interfaces and values without relying on the existing code path. Since there would be multiple object paths needed to dump the information.

But that can be solved by having some small helper program to dump the subtree  and it's dbus interfaces without the 
```
org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable
org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer
org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties
```
which seems to be on all the object paths.

Would you like to have such a helper program created to make the workflow easier?

## concern about performance (daemon consuming the config)

When using the new API, there may be more DBus calls required than before.
Since the information is found on different object paths instead of one.

I would not be too concerned since the configuration may not change that often.

## concern about performance (EM)

Would you like to see some benchmarks here? We could insert some timestamp logging into EM at debug level to make it easier to look at the impacts of changes like that.

I really appreciate this is documented!

Could you please integrate this with the existing docs on the topic, so we don't have to maintain both?

This seems to be in design doc format, so it might be useful in the design doc folder in its own review?  Regardless, we should update the config format docs in the em repo (once we've agreed on what the format is).

> Could you please integrate this with the existing docs on the topic, so we don't have to maintain both?

If we can make the transition, we could just delete the other doc. If there is a time when both ways will work then having both documents may help to conceptually separate the 2 representations.

> This seems to be in design doc format, so it might be useful in the design doc folder in its own review?

In case there are alternatives to consider, or opportunity to get input from wider community, yes, but in this case i do not see many design choices.
At least not anything that would make sense to me.

From my perspective it boils down to "how to map json to DBus". The nesting (objects and arrays) then has to be represented in either dbus names, object paths, interfaces or properties (and their values).

We can not use dbus names, properties or interfaces for the nesting since they are not intended to be used that way. Properties should be the same for different instances of a dbus interface, so they cannot represent arrays. DBus names should be unique and traditionally services only have one name. So they cannot be used.
Multiple DBus interfaces with different names (which have the same properties) are also not good for the code and hard to re-use.

Putting the nesting in the property type and value would make it hard to work with since the property names (from the nested json) will be lost.


Then only object paths remain to represent the nesting.

@spinler@us.ibm.com @patrick@stwcx.xyz Do you think we need to go through the design doc process for this feature?

> If we can make the transition, we could just delete the other doc

Would really prefer to see one integrated doc.  There's content in the other doc that is still relevant even in this design.

I FWIW don't really need a design, but would like to see concrete examples using non-abstract exposes types.
